entry.title: Hum Are Hitting the Road in 2027
entry.summary: It’s the Illinois rock band’s first proper run since 2015
entry.content:
Veteran Illinois shoegaze band Hum have announced a 2027 tour, their first proper run since 2015. The U.S. treck kicks off in Atlanta in March, stopping in Austin, Philadelphia, New York, Boston, Seattle, and more before concluding in San Francisco in July. All dates will feature support from Kansas City’s the Life and Times, while Chicago post-hardcore band Pelican and Brooklyn trio Spotlights will open on East and West Coast dates, respectively. Check out a full itinerary below.

The shows build upon Hum’s well-received headlining sets earlier this year at traveling shoegaze festival Slide Away, where they shared top billing with Chapterhouse and Nothing. Those dates were Hum’s first shows in nearly seven years, a hiatus that also encompassed the death of original drummer Bryan St. Pere in 2021. Shiner’s Jason Gerken, who joined the group on drums during their 2015 tour and at Slide Away, will return to the kit for the forthcoming dates.

Hum’s Slide Away sets marked the first time the band performed songs from their 2020 album Inlet live. Prior to that release, they hadn’t shared a record since 1997’s Downward Is Heavenward, which followed 1995’s You’d Prefer An Astronaut and their 1993 debut Electra 2000.

entry.title: Neil Young Really Wants Trump to Stop Playing “Rockin’ in the Free World”
entry.summary: He’s suing (again) over the president’s unauthorized use of the song at political rallies
entry.content:
Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Neil Young is filing suit after “Rockin’ in the Free World” was played at a Trump rally. The lawsuit—filed yesterday (Monday, October 26) in Virginia’s Eastern District Court—specifically cites an “unauthorized public performance” of Young’s 1991 protest anthem at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio on October 12. The named defendant is actually not President Donald J. Trump himself, but rather the Trump 47 Committee, his primary political action committee and the event’s organizer.

“‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ is a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless, and forgotten,” the lawsuit reads. “The lyrics paint vivid, street-level portraits—a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity—while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn’t shared by all. In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for.” Pitchfork has reached out to Young’s legal representation for further comment.

Young is seeking $10 million in damages on the grounds of copyright infringement, asserting that the Trump 47 Committee did not have “license or Young’s permission” to play the song at any “purely political event.” He also demands that neither “Rockin’ in the Free World” nor any of his other songs be played at future events organized by or associated with the PAC.

During the 2020 presidential election, Young sued Trump’s campaign committee, Donald J. Trump for President Inc., over their use of “Rockin’ in the Free World” and another of his songs, “Devil’s Sidewalk,” at campaign rallies. The parties settled out of court under the stipulation, according to the new suit, that the corporation “would never use ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ without a license and permission from Young.” However, as a separate organization, the Trump 47 Committee would be exempt from the terms of that specific settlement. Agh, technicalities!

entry.title: Listen to MJ Lenderman Cover Lambchop’s “Weakened”
entry.summary: From the veteran Nashville band's new covers EP Demoed
entry.content:
MJ Lenderman has added yet another killer cover to his catalog, this time of alt-country heroes Lambchop’s song “Weakened.” The original appears on the Kurt Wagner-fronted band’s August album Punching the Clown; the new version features Lenderman singing, playing bass; and guitar alongside Fog’s Andrew Broder.

Lenderman’s take on “Weakened” appears on Lambchop’s forthcoming EP Demoed, a collection of demo covers of songs from Punching the Clown. Wagner primarily recruited younger musicians to take up the mantle, including Lauren Auder, Circuit des Yeux and Alan Sparhawk, Flock of Dimes, and More Eaze. The full EP is due November 20 digitally, and February 5 physically.

“I used to fantasize that Lambchop would continue as an idea well beyond my participation,” Wagner shared in press materials. “Over time we’ve had at least two generations represented. A third now is beginning. And this is important to me, having the unique perspective and contributions from younger artists steering in the work we make. So I thought it would be nice, someday, that I might even step aside to watch and advise from the wings. Having a beard was never considered, but here we are.”

Lenderman dropped his most recent solo album, Manning Fireweworks, in 2024. Last year, he released a live album with Karly Hartzman recorded at Nashville’s Third Man Records. Since then, he’s also released a song with This is Lorelei, and spent this past spring on tour with Waxahatchee.

entry.title: Shelved David Bowie Concert Film Revived for Immersive Live Show
entry.summary: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen has remastered the unreleased 1978 film “Stage” for a multi-screen extravaganza
entry.content:
The unreleased David Bowie concert film “Stage”, recorded on his 1978 tour behind Low and “Heroes”, will tour arenas as a novel multimedia experience in 2027. Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen has adapted footage from Bowie’s Isolar II tour—originally shot by David Hemmings—for a multi-screen live show, also called “Stage”. It will premiere at Berlin’s Uber Arena on February 14 before further, as-yet-unannounced shows. Watch a trailer below.

Morgen originally conceived the project in 2018, while sifting Bowie’s archives for his 2022 documentary. (Hemmings’ footage of “Heroes”, the song, made the cut of Moonage Daydream.) Bowie had intended Hemmings’ film from Earls Court, in London, to play in unorthodox spaces, such as live venues, as an alternative to touring himself, The Guardian notes. In the end, Bowie released a live album, 1978’s Stage, but shelved the footage to focus on other projects; he also quit touring until 1983. “I simply didn’t like the way [Hemmings’ footage] had been shot,” Bowie told Uncut in 2001. “Now, of course, it looks pretty good and I would suspect that it would make it out some time in the future.”

Morgen spent years meticulously remastering Hemmings’ 35mm film and configuring it for multiple screens. The event will feature an integrated lighting show from Patrick Woodroffe and immersive audio mixed by Paul Massey. The elaborate LED displays and audio mix, the press release notes, are designed for “auditoriums and venues with capacities starting at 5,000, enveloping audiences in the atmosphere of a full-scale rock concert.” Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld and the David Bowie Estate also collaborated on the project.

entry.title: Factory Floor Return With First Album in 10 Years
entry.summary: Listen to “Continuation” and the title track from One Trip
entry.content:
Factory Floor, the London electronic outfit that released its buzzy debut on DFA in 2013, are back with a new album, One Trip. The double single “Continuation” / “One Trip” leads the first LP in a decade from the trio, now comprising original members Nik Colk Void and Gabe Gurnsey with new addition Joe Ward. They will bring a new live show to London Barbican, supporting Squid, on December 5. Listen to the new songs below ahead of the album release on November 27.

Factory Floor originally included Dominic Butler, who exited before second album 25 25 arrived in 2016. Gurnsey and Void continued to release music on labels such as Editions Mego and Erol Alkan’s Phantasy Sound, the latter of which is also putting out the new record following a string of recent singles.

The band returned in 2024 at Mutek Festival. After that performance, they said in a press release, “We felt an appetite to work in a space where artists could connect emotionally and physically, both in the studio and on a live stage. These environments hold more than sound; they carry a visceral energy that comes from being together. It’s something we’d really missed as solo artists, and it made us want to explore that kind of experience again.”

entry.title: Dead Man’s Bones Unveil First New Song in 17 Years
entry.summary: The duo of Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields return with “Lost in the Night”
entry.content:
After a short teaser clip lit up the internet with news of their return, Dead Man’s Bones—the duo of Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields—are officially back with their first new music in 17 years. “Lost in the Night” was produced with longtime collaborator Tim Anderson, and it gets a black-and-white music video starring Hamnet’s Noah Jupe and The Summer I Turned Pretty’s Rain Spencer that draws on its lovestruck lyrics. Check it out below.

Dead Man’s Bones set out to write new music in recent years, but couldn‘t settle on where to record it. The duo tried a number of Los Angeles studios before driving to a farm outside of the city with some gear in tow—two guitars, two drum machines, and two synthesizers—where they proceeded to record “Lost in the Night” in one day.

The first and only Dead Man’s Bones album came out in 2009. Gosling and Shields worked closely with the Silverlake Conservatory Children’s Choir, a California education organization founded by Flea, on their self-titled debut to achieve its cross of indie rock, gothic folk, and doo-wop. The duo retreated from the public eye after promoting their first album. However, they found renewed interest over the years through covers (like Cat Power tackling “Pa Pa Power” for her 2022 album Covers), various film and TV syncs, and a seasonal bump courtesy of social media users playing their music around Halloween.

Revisit Rob Mitchum’s review of Dead Man’s Bones.

entry.title: Jay-Z Confirmed for Super Bowl 2027 Halftime Show
entry.summary: The Roc Nation founder will headline his own event at California’s SoFi Stadium on Valentine’s Day
entry.content:
Jay-Z, the founder of the company that books the Super Bowl halftime show, has found his 2027 headliner: himself. The Roc Nation chief will perform at the event for the first time for next year’s Super Bowl LXI. The game takes place on February 14, Valentine’s Day, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. ESPN is televising the game for the first time, and, for the first time since 2006, ABC is also airing it. Check out Jay-Z’s teaser clip for the halftime show below.

Jay-Z has been the NFL’s live music entertainment strategist since 2019 and also operates as a producer with final say on the headliner. In 2024, asked if he would ever headline the show himself, he told Entertainment Tonight, “I thought it would be selfish to pick myself too early. Maybe one year. Maybe.”

In a press release sent tonight announcing his billing, Jay-Z had this to say: “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey. Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

Today’s announcement by Roc Nation follows last year’s Bad Bunny show, which drew vitriol from the far-right, including President Trump, and support from a huge swath of the music world and other politicians.

Revisit E.R. Pulgar’s review Bad Bunny’s Incredible Super Bowl Halftime Show Planted a New Flag.

entry.title: Sufjan Stevens Makes First Live Appearance in Over Eight Years
entry.summary: He played piano at Meg Lui’s show in Kingston, New York
entry.content:
Last month, Sufjan Stevens made a surprise onstage appearance during Meg Lui’s show at Tempo in Kingston, New York. Stevens accompanied the singer-songwriter on piano and backing vocals for her song “Elvis Queen,” taken from her new album Instant Validation, which Stevens produced. It marked his first public musical performance in over eight years. Back in 2023, Stevens revealed he was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome—a rare auto-immune disorder in which the body’s immune system attacks the nerves—and was working to relearn how to walk and use his hands. Watch a clip from the performance below.

This September 25 concert was Lui’s record release event for Instant Validation, which came out that same day via Asthmatic Kitty Records. Although it’s technically her debut album, the Hudson Valley-based singer-songwriter has written music before and worked with Stevens in the past; she contributed background vocals to his most recent album, 2023’s Javelin. The two met through mutual friends in the Catskills and recorded Instant Validation at Stevens’ home studio. “With Sufjan there was so much more out-of-the-box thinking, and we ended up adding layers upon layers that created an unrestrained soundscape for the record,” Lui previously said of the experience.

Last year, Stevens said he was doing “okay” in an interview with Vulture’s Craig Jenkins. “I’ve had some pretty difficult things happen to me, so I’m in a state of repair and survival,” Stevens elaborated. “I’m not really in any state of mind or any position to go on tour yet. But I’m starting to see the light. I’m starting to feel a sense of direction toward something meaningful and substantial. I’ve been focusing on the moment and on things that feel very silly and Zen: serenity and acceptance and duty and stewardship.”

In the years following his diagnosis, Stevens reissued a 20th anniversary edition of Seven Swans and a 10th anniversary version of Carrie & Lowell, he produced a children’s album for John Legend, and the musical Illinoise—which was based off his 2005 album Illinois—won a Tony Award. Stevens has also hopped on new songs by Mina Tindle and Mouse on Mars’ Jan St. Werner. These days, he’s busy taking a more hands-on approach at his label Asthmatic Kitty and in his backyard garden at home.

Read about Javelin at No. 6 in The 50 Best Albums of 2023.

entry.title: The Flaming Lips Reveal New Album The Teardrop Throbs
entry.summary: The announcement arrives with a 2,300-word post from Wayne Coyne
entry.content:
Two months after they drop the 20th anniversary edition of At War With the Mystics, The Flaming Lips will return with their first new album in seven years (and 17th in total). The Teardrop Throbs, the band’s debut on Third Man Records, arrives January 22. The release also marks the psych-rockers first LP in 35 years to not feature multi-instrumentalist Steven Drozd, who is no longer in the band (reasons for why vary depending on the party). Teardrop is led by single “God Will Control the Werewolves”—which you can listen to below—along with a sequel to Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots’ “Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell.”

“I’ve always liked it when songs from previous records get a new rendering,” Coyne said about “Ego Tripping Part Two” in a very long, grammatically insane statement accompanying the release (you can read the full 2,000-plus word missive below). “It’s not the same song but it is dealing with Ego death.. what is status and power and the struggle to turn it into something useful..and this again is an attempt to capture the idea of Syd Barrett fronting Pink Floyd and instead of singing about money ( Money was a big single off Dark Side Of The Moon) he , Syd, chooses to sing about a queen killing the king and stealing his crown to melt it down and make sword out of it ..ha!!!”

Following its release, Coyne and co. will present The Teardrop Throbs—which was produced by the band alongside Taylor Johnson, Dave Fridmann, and Scott Booker, with additional production by Jon and Mike Fridmann—at a handful of intimate shows. Those dates are also listed below.

Revisit our 2020 review of the Lips’ American Head.

The Teardrop Throbs:
01 Throb
02 God Will Control the Werewolves
03 Titan
04 Every Teardrop Cried
05 Hooray
06 Instructions On How to Draw An Eyeball or How To Deal With a Loved One Who Is Addicted to Drugs
07 You See You In Me
08 You’ve Got Brain Damage
09 At the End of the Day
10 The Trees Are Getting Their Leaves / Ceasefire in the City of Singing Flame
11 Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell Part Two
12 A Sunset Far Away
13 Now I Understand

Flaming Lips: The Teardrop Throbs
$26.99 at Rough Trade

Wayne Coyne:

I was sitting in the car in the Trader Joe’s parking lot. Little Rex was 3 years old at that time and he was sleeping in the backseat. I would check on him looking in the rearview mirror. And ( like all fathers with little kids ) was astonished at how beautiful and perfect he was and if anything happened to him ( like illness or bad accident) my life would be destroyed.. I think all parents probably have these types of thoughts a hundred times every day. So with these things floating around my head I noticed a sign ( for I guess one of the establishments in the strip mall:: that the Trader Joe’s was in) .. it read Children’s Death Foundation… I immediately thought of my mother , as a teenager ,assisting  the nuns at her Catholic junior high school with grieving families that had just suffered the loss of a child. I imagined the cold nights sitting with strangers consoling and understanding them and attempting to hold their family together…it was just my imagination running away with me and I looked up again at little Rex in the backseat and again at this sign..I had mis-read it .. it actually said Children’s HEALTH Foundation not Children’s DEATH Foundation …I had done that a couple other times where , I guess, I had death on my mind . I remember being at the State Fair and seeing Funnel Cakes as Funeral Cakes .. but this flash of my mother volunteering at the Children’s Death Foundation had solidified in my mind and already moved me so, even though I was wrong the damage or the epiphany had already been done.

It occurred to me there will never be anything in my life as important as my two little boys.. So.. I am lucky. To have arrived at the greatest of the greatest purposes in life ..yes.. I am here. But also we ( The Flaming Lips ) are making a new record and what’s in your mind usually finds its way into your music whether you intend it to or not .The first song on this new record was also the first song that presented itself in this 2 year process.

The song Throb is a snippet from the soundtrack to the movie The Night of the Hunter.. I always loved the music in this movie and especially the Pretty Fly song that the little girl sings as her and her brother float down the river having just escaped being kidnapped by the evil preacher guy. I had set A.J. ( Adam Judd Slaughter) our new slide guitar player (he can actually play everything including drums) to task of doing a note for note re-playing of the Pretty Fly song and he did a long beginning and a long end that I didn’t recognize.. but it was really evocative.. and so without knowing where this would go we began to put some guitars and drum machines to it ..it was a longer piece of music that included the Pretty Fly song that I changed the lyrics to ( about a dreary hospital ) and this small section is all that survived ( for now ) and it was in keeping with the Children’s Death Foundation vision I had .. the movie The Night of the Hunter is really a  nightmare about children in peril..

The second track God Will Control the Werewolves started as a little story about my 2 boys ( Bloom and Rex) and me playing hide and seek at the park as it was getting dark outside. We had all become very aware of the moon cycles when we stayed at an ocean view Airbnb about a month previous . The full moon had sucked all the water out of this ocean cove area and we walked a quarter mile out in the seabed seeing strange ocean creatures attached to the rocks .. but yes.. because of the moon we had this amazing adventure so it was fresh in our minds and on this evening of hide and seek it was luckily another full moon.. Bloom asked me if, while him and Rex were hiding , the werewolves would get them ( they had also watched a few werewolf movies and knew that the full moon was the time when the werewolves were out and about ) and I told him God would control the werewolves for a little bit while we played hide n seek.. The way I heard the song sounding ( in my head ) was kind of Pink Floyd Dark Side Of The Moon BUT Syd Barrett is still in the band .. ha..

The third track was a throbbing little song that Tommy ( our bass player ) cooked up on his home Pro-Tools rig .. when it arrived it was called .. I think .. Matrix .. it was menacing but also kind of hyper and it was a fun mood to insert right after the slow dark God Will Control the Werewolves track. We added some Mellotron flutes and an awkward chord break in the middle. And left it alone for a bit . And then one morning I was walking to the Tim Hortons down the road from Dave Fridmann’s studio ( it’s almost 2 miles there) and I had this song ( this Matrix song ) running through my head and I had my phone out and I got a text from Perry Farrell.. he sent a little poem about ( hold on let me find the text ) being like a frog and jumping from one idea of life to another .. jump lightly and don’t mess up your lillypads .. ( how great is that !!) and I was reminded of his crazy intense singing ( like Coming Down The Mountain.. that song ) and pictured a high energetic voice screaming some advice about taking action !! The Frogs are Jumping oh oh!! The Sun’s eruptin let’s go!! The Titans are hunting !! The stars are melting Let’s go!!! Matt did some amazing high singing and Improvising that really opened up a new melodic sense that The Flaming Lips hadn’t played with before.

The next track Every Teardrop Cried started as just one line .. it was meant to be just an interlude between songs .. it started that day in the Trader Joe’s parking lot ..the line was “Every drop of rain that falls is you…” referring again to the death of a child ( a believe it had been about a year since Nell had died ) seeing this child in every thing that is sublime .. and I thought one line really summed it up..but I couldn’t stop and added another line and another ..the middle verse “you’re in my eyes”.. “you’re in my ears”. “and when I cry you’re in my tears” .. when i sang it , i think i wrote it and sang at the same time .. It seemed like a song that had already been around forever .

The song Hooray started out being connected to the song At The End of the Day .. but quickly became too big and we trimmed it down and made it two songs instead of one big long song . It started out as a Sci-Fi / Spy adventure type song. It was originally about a blonde secret agent super-freak woman and she steals the president’s brain and is on the run from some futuristic Russian assassins..Katy my wife heard it and thought .. this sounded so sweet and longing ( she was listening from another room) and now that I hear the words and realize you’re singing about the president’s brain.. you must change it .. people will think you’re talking about Trump and it’s too beautiful to have anyone think of Trump .. you must change it ..ha.. so .. of course I changed it ..

The song Instructions on how to draw an eyeball or how to deal with a loved one who is addicted to drugs is a simple simple song that I kind of made up as I sang it into the microphone. “I don’t know why but I just keep on trying again and again”.. it’s a mantra mostly .. like something you tell yourself hoping that it’s true.

The song You See You in Me .. these great little splatters of guitar rhythms ( with lyrics) da da da dada da da“ There one goes!!! Dadada (kind of machine gun) Another one goes” made us all laugh. That the song would really do that..Using the song structure as sound effect to tell the story.. The original take of the song went a couple minutes longer at the end.  With A.J’s slide guitars getting crunchier as it went and the distorted string patch that Derek played .getting more and more distorted..we couldn’t decide where to stop.. luckily some time passed and eventually we were with Dave Fridmann and without any struggle we made the song a few minutes shorter and added to the very end an unexpected message “the flames reach higher”

Sometimes there is an energy when a song is being made that is in the actual MAKING of it and upon LISTENING later you understand that.. the energy is NOT in the listening …so.. making it shorter kept the song alive instead of it running out of steam as it built. But these are the mechanisms of recording that I sometimes fear can take the magic out of a song.. to think of a song as drum parts and string parts and bass parts all haphazardly thrown together maybe does the song a disservice. This song has some kind of pure enthusiasm that you can’t really put into words.

The song You’ve Got Brain Damage is, I believe, the first song I wrote that signaled we were making a new album. A.J. had a simple droning chord progression that I heard on his Bandcamp album and I asked him if I could turn it into a song . I went to his house and we chopped up that song ( on his home Pro-Tools set up) and I sang over top of it. I had been ruminating late into the previous night about drugs and alcohol causing brain damage. Just thinking about all the humans I’ve known who have fucked themselves up and how sad it is.. how some people are just beyond help and nothing can reach them .. and hoping I haven’t done that to myself..or that I NEVER do that to myself … jeez.. but maybe I’m damaged and I don’t realize it.. like maybe my oldest brother dosed me with some potent LSD micro-dot when I was 8 years old and I never came down and this my long long hallucination of my life and my body is actually laying in some forgotten medical bed and I’m just drooling on myself twitching from paranoia… jeez.. if it’s true don’t wake me …

The track At The End of the Day started out as a song with lyrics and melody .. I was playing guitar and singing in my kitchen and Katy ( my wonderful wife) she began singing this line “At the end of the day”…. I quickly turned it into a little song about how in the fall the shadows of the oncoming evening make you melancholy and slightly depressed but also kind of a comforting distress .. the trees are dying :: you are dying :: the sun is dying …we began to add some instrumentation to this little chord progression and it quickly revealed itself ( the song did ) as more powerful WITHOUT my narration..

I still feel like I will return to it someday..

The song The Trees Are Getting Their Leaves ( Ceasefire in The City of The Singing Flame) .. this is an imaginary city street and I am witnessing all the new life emerging from the end of the war.. “The trees are getting their leaves .. the cold burst violence is over.. the flowers melted the screams .. the Holy Virgin’s Transmitting”… the holy virgin ( in my story ) is an underground radio station that was broadcasting a freedom poem on endless loop..

This segues into Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell Part 2::: .. I’ve always liked it when songs from previous records ( Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell is a song off of our 2002 album Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots) get a new rendering .. it’s not the same song but it is dealing with Ego death.. what is status and power and the struggle to turn it into something useful..and this again is an attempt to capture the idea of Syd Barrett fronting Pink Floyd and instead of singing about money ( Money was a big single off Dark Side Of The Moon) he , Syd, chooses, instead of singing about money to sing about a queen killing the king and stealing his crown to melt it down and make sword out of it ..ha!!!

The long ending of Ego Tripping at the Gates of Hell Part 2 dissolves into the beginning of A Sunset Far Away. A Sunset Far Away is probably about some beautiful but tumultuous situation that is better left in the distance ..and to still feel optimistic about it .. ha.. the middle section lingers as the voice from beyond watches the sun go down down down down .. lower and lower ..

The last track is an instrumental called Now I Understand is the orchestration that was behind an ending of another song ..we discarded ( for now ) the song structure and singing and drums and guitars and for The Teardrop Throbs presented it as this cosmic drama that seems to have a happy resolve ..

.. so .. dear reader .. please keep in mind there are a thousand things that go into making a song .. I don’t really believe any song has a fixed meaning .. and I don’t WANT my songs to have a fixed meaning .. I think the song should be allowed to affect your mood and feelings regardless of how we ( as The Flaming Lips) played it and put it together..these notes are just some talking points to help make it easy to have some insight that you can use when reviewing and discussing this album ..

I am glad to talk about anything you are interested in..

Love love love

Wayne 2026

entry.title: Ecco2K, Whait, Angelo LeRoi, and More: This Week’s Pitchfork Selects Playlist
entry.summary: Our weekly playlist highlights songs that our writers, editors, and contributors are listening to on repeat
entry.content:
The staff of Pitchfork listens to a lot of new music. A lot of it. On any given day our writers, editors, and contributors go through an imposing number of new releases, giving recommendations to each other and discovering new favorites along the way. Each Monday, with our Pitchfork Selects playlist, we’re sharing what our writers are playing obsessively and highlighting some of the Pitchfork staff’s favorite new music. The playlist is a grab-bag of tracks: Its only guiding principle is that these are the songs you’d gladly send to a friend.

entry.title: The Weeknd Debuts “Hong Kong” in Hong Kong
entry.summary: Faye Wong features on the new song, premiered during his four-night run at Kai Tak Stadium
entry.content:
Opening a four-night run at Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong, the Weeknd debuted the thematically apt “Hong Kong” on Saturday. The new song features the Hong Kong singer-songwriter and actor Faye Wong, who also stars in a sleek visual accompaniment, set in the nation’s capital. You can watch the performance below.

Earlier this year, the Weeknd premiered another metropolis-themed song, “Rio,” in the titular city (that one was a duet with Anitta, who previously joined Tesfaye on “São Paulo”) along with a track that sampled the theme from Neon Genesis Evangelion. His previous album, Hurry Up Tomorrow, came out last February.

entry.title: Throwing Muses Reissue Self-Titled Debut Album for 40th Anniversary
entry.summary: Throwing Muses introduced 4AD’s first American signing to the world
entry.content:
Rhode Island indie rock legends Throwing Muses will reissue their long-out-of-print (and off streaming) self-titled debut this December, in honor of its 40th anniversary. The new edition of Throwing Muses, due December 11 on 4AD, celebrates the first full-length album by the first American band ever signed by the label, a major inflection point in its history.

The quartet of of vocalist Kristin Hersh, guitarist-vocalist Tanya Donelly, bassist Leslie Langston, and drummer David Narcizo were still teenagers when they released Throwing Muses in 1986. The album largely drew inspiration from a car accident that left a 16-year-old Hersh, the band’s primary lyricist, with a rod in her skull. In the aftermath, she says she began hallucinating songs like the snarling tracks Throwing Muses would eventually release.

“I can’t even remember what it was like to hear a song that didn’t grab my face and shout at it,” Hersh wrote in her 2010 memoir Rat Girl. “Must’ve been soothing. But this is electrifying.”

After 4AD signed Throwing Muses, the label’s direction shifted towards American alternative rock, exemplified by their signing of the Pixies in 1987. Throwing Muses went on to release seven albums and two EPs on 4AD. Their most LP was 2025’s Moonlight Concessions. The group has also spawned multiple side projects, including 50FootWave and Lakuna.

Revisit Katherine St. Asaph’s Sunday Review of Throwing Muses.

entry.title: Elvis Presley Catalog Owners Sue AI Company Anthropic for Copyright Infringement
entry.summary: The lawsuit claims Anthropic illegally used 274 songs by The King to train its AI model Claude
entry.content:
The licensing group that owns the rights to Elvis Presley’s music and license has filed a $41 million lawsuit against AI company Anthropic. The Tennessee-based Authentic Brands Group alleges that Anthropic infringed on their copyright by training its AI model Claude on 274 of Presley’s songs without permission, including “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “Don’t Be Cruel,” “Farther Along,” “If You Think I Don’t Need You,” and “Run On.”

The lawsuit, filed on October 23 and viewed by Pitchfork, seeks roughly $150,000 in damages per song, adding up to $41 million. Authentic Brands Group filed alongside a number of co-plaintiffs with ownership over Presley rights. “The Elvis Plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,” lead attorney Richard Busch wrote in a statement. “The Elvis Plaintiffs are deeply protective of these iconic songs.” Pitchfork has reached out to representatives for Anthropic for comment.

Although major labels and music publishers have filed claims against Anthropic before, Authentic Brands Group’s lawsuit is one of the first high-profile cases wherein the owner of a single artist’s catalog sued for copyright infringement. The lawsuit claims that Anthropic has illegally used the aforementioned Presley songs to create “unlicensed derivative works” with Claude.

“Even after the Defendant supposedly put up ‘guardrails’ after being sued, in one of its latest iterations, Claude continues to infringe: when recently asked to recreate specific songs ‘for a modern audience,’ Claude did so and admitted: ‘These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges,” the lawsuit reads. “That’s edging past ‘inspired by’ into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out.’”

entry.title: Watch Jay-Z Bring Out Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg at LA Tour Closer
entry.summary: Too $hort, John Legend, Scarface, and Blue Ivy Carter also joined the final Jay-Z 30 shows at SoFi Stadium
entry.content:
Jay-Z closed out his Jay-Z 30 tour this weekend at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, bringing an end to a headlining run that broke Yankee Stadium’s ticket sales record and featured guest appearances from Nas, The-Dream, Rihanna, and Beyoncé. The tour celebrated the 30th anniversary of Jay’s debut album Reasonable Doubt, and kicked off earlier this year with a headlining show at Philadelphia’s Roots Picnic.

On Friday, October 23, he invited Scarface to the stage to rap “This Can’t Be Life” and “Mind Playing Tricks on Me.” Following with prior tour stops, Jay’s daughter, Blue Ivy Carter, accompanied him on piano during “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents / Dead Presidents II.” After ending his main set with “Public Service Announcement,” he returned to the stage for an encore with two more guests: John Legend and DJ Khaled, who joined him in a performance of their eight-plus-minute song “God Did."

The second and final night of the tour saw Jay-Z joined by Too $hort for a medley of his well-known “Blow the Whistle Freestyle” and the original 2006 “Blow the Whistle.” But the marquee guest spot of the evening featured Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg, both of whom came out to perform a medley of hits including “The Next Episode,” “Still Dre,” “Nuthin But a G Thang,” and of course, “California Love.” Jay also took the opportunity to honor late Los Angeles rapper Nipsey Hussle, who was killed in a 2019 shooting. He projected a black-and-white photo of the artist while playing his song “Hussle & Motivate,“ then incorporated the rapper’s “Last Time That I Checc'd” into a performance of “On to the Next One.”

During the tour closer, Jay-Z also took a moment to address criticism of the tour, specifically around alleged low-priced resale tickets, circulating online. ”Y’all gotta be very aware of what’s going on in the world, right? People will tell you that nobody was in here tonight, but you got eyes, you can see. People will tell you that the music wasn’t great, but you got ears,” he said. “You gotta understand, you gotta question everything in this world of AI.”

entry.title: Turnstile Pack Out Washington Monument for Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon Benefit Show
entry.summary: The Baltimore hardcore band raised over $220,000 for Human Concern International’s relief efforts in the three regions
entry.content:
Turnstile took over the National Lawn in Washington, D.C. on October 24 with a massive free show raising funds for Human Concern International’s relief efforts in Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon. The benefit concert concluded Turnstile’s second North American tour in support of their Grammy-winning album Never Enough. Check out footage from the show—and a full set list—below.

Per the Baltimore Banner, the first two fans in line for the 3 p.m. show arrived at the National Lawn at 5:00 a.m. All told, the National Park Service estimated that around 60,000 people were in the crowd. Turnstile aimed to raise $150,000 for Human Concern International; as of this writing, the show’s official LaunchGood page has raised over $221,000.

At the middle of the set, frontman Brendan Yates thanked the crowd for showing out and supporting their cause, telling the crowd, “We’re so grateful to have been raised by this scene, one that taught us that music not only reflects the artist making it but the people and the world and the suffering and the joy that surrounds it.” He concluded by leading a chant: “Loud enough for the White House to hear it: Free Palestine! Free Sudan! Free Lebanon!”

The Washington Monument benefit show marked Turnstile’s biggest yet, but it’s not the first time they’ve played free of charge for a good cause. In 2025, the Baltimore band hosted a hometown show in Wyman Park Dell to raise money for the nonprofit Health Care for the Homeless, a Maryland nonprofit that provides medical care and housing assistance for people experiencing homelessness. They funded the production out of pocket, and the show raised over $35,000 for the organization.

The Saturday show only added to the list of milestones Turnstile has accomplished this year. In February, the band won their first two Grammy Awards, for Best Rock Album (for Never Enough) and Best Metal Performance (for “Birds”). They made history that night as the first band to earn nominations across the Rock, Metal, and Alternative music categories. In August, they released an album of Never Enough remixes, with features from Elton John, Panda Bear, Hayley Williams, Oklou, Slayyyter, Chanel Beads, and more. Just this month, they also made their Saturday Night Live debut, becoming the first hardcore group to play Studio 8H since 1981.

This year, however, has not been without its trials. In March, the band’s former guitarist Brady Ebert was arrested for attempted murder after allegedly hitting Yates’ father with his car. William Yates was hospitalized after suffering “severe physical trauma” to his legs in the alleged attack, the band said in a statement to Pitchfork. The band parted ways with Ebert in 2022, noting in their statement that this decision was made "in response to a consistent pattern of harmful behavior affecting himself, the band, and the community.” The statement concluded, ”We have no language left for Brady.”

Although Turnstile’s ’s Washington Monument show concluded the Never Enough tour, they already have a few forthcoming festival dates lined up. They’ll play Tyler, the Creator’s Camp Flog Gnaw Carnival in November, and have also been confirmed to Primavera Sound’s 2027 bill.

Learn all about Turnstile’s rise in Lawrence Burney’s cover story Turnstile Blew Up. Now What?

entry.title: Slayyyter Cancels Remaining UK and European Tour Dates
entry.summary: Laryngitis and vocal cord tears are forcing the singer “to go on medication and full vocal rest for at least two weeks”
entry.content:
Slayyyter is calling off the last shows of her ongoing UK and European tour on doctor's orders. In an Instagram story viewed by Pitchfork, the pop singer wrote, “I am heartbroken to share after multiple doctor visits i have laryngitis and vocal cord tears,” adding, “Because of this, i am forced to cancel the remaining UK/EU dates to avoid permanent damage to my voice.” Among the scrapped Wor$t Girl in America tour stops are Copenhagen, Hamburg, Warsaw, Prague, Berlin, Antwerp, Manchester, Birmingham, Glasgow, Brighton, and London. Slayyyter has promised full refunds to fans and is “already working on rebooking shows for next year.” You can read her full note below.

Speaking of next year, Slayyyter is still slated to play dates in 2027 across Australia, New Zealand, and South America. Before that, she’ll debut her Wor$t Girl companion album, Wor$t Man in America, on December 4.

Slayyyter:

hey guys, i am heartbroken to share after multiple doctor visits i have laryngitis and vocal cord tears and have been ordered to go on medication and full vocal rest for at least two weeks. Because of this, i am forced to cancel the remaining UK/EU dates to avoid permanent damage to my voice. full refunds will be available at point of sale.

my team and i are already working on rebooking shows for next year and i hope to have news to share very soon to make it up to you. I know how much time and effort is spent to come out to a show. some of you have traveled, some of you have made costumes, and i am completely devastated to not be able to give you the shows you were planning for. we are working hard to figure out a time to return so i can deliver an even bigger and better show for you all. i hope you know i will make this up to you . lots of love to you all. thank you for making this tour so spcial.”

entry.title: Noel Gallagher Talks Vegans, Macca, Underwear on Chicken Shop Date
entry.summary: “Do you know what’s not a high-flying bird? A chicken.”
entry.content:
“Do you know what’s not a high-flying bird? A chicken.” Noel Gallagher is the latest guest on Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Chicken Shop Date. In the new episode, the elder Gallagher brother opines on vegetarians (“Fuck those guys”), Macca (“He’s one of those rare people that when you meet him, you walk away from it feeling good about yourself”), and the long-standing rumor—started by him, mind you—that he doesn’t wear underwear onstage: “That’s nonsense—I wear two pairs of underpants.”

Throughout the clip, Dimoldenberg peppers Gallagher with her characteristically acerbic questions. Asked “how do you make a comeback feel natural and not desperate,” he replies, “You can’t make sure, you just gotta hope that you can do whatever it is you’re trying to do as well as you once did it. And in the case of Oasis, it became apparent after maybe a week in rehearsals that it was gonna be as good—if not better—than it ever was.”

At another point, Gallagher addresses that inscrutable “Champagne Supernova” lyric: “I mean, I’ve still no idea what ‘slowly walking down the hall/Faster than a cannonball’ means. Do you?” “Well, it means you’re walking quite fast,” Dimoldenberg replies, to which Gallagher counters, “I think it’s a drug reference.” The two also engage in some light football banter (Gallagher famously supports Man City, while Dimoldenberg is a United fan). Watch the full segment below.

After a 12-year run, Chicken Shop Date is winding down with its final season. Role Model and Jorja Smith have also made recent appearances on the show. Meanwhile, the second coming of Oasis will proceed apace well into 2027, with live dates across Europe, the UK, and the U.S. slated through September. Next month the band will be honored at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony.

entry.title: Chappell Roan Duets With Caroline Polachek, PinkPantheress, and Lola Young
entry.summary: All on the closing night of Roan’s Los Angeles pop extravaganza, the Super Graphic Spectacular
entry.content:
Midwest Princess Chappell Roan anointed a dynasty of fellow royals to close out her two-night benefit concert in Los Angeles last night. Held at Shrine Auditorium, the Super Graphic Spectacular celebrated the first anniversary of Roan’s Midwest Princess Project, which supports young people from LGBTQ+ communities. After joining Caroline Polachek to do “Look at Me Now,” Roan stepped up for a headline set with surprise guests PinkPantheress (doing “Tonight”) and Lola Young (“Picture You”).

On Wednesday night, Roan’s first headline set of the extravaganza featured a surprise appearance from Christina Aguilera. For good measure, Roan also joined Charli XCX for “Boom Clap” at Kia Forum last weekend.

entry.title: Haywire Set Jam-Packed 2027 Tour
entry.summary: The Boston hardcore outfit will play a whopping 80 shows between January and April
entry.content:
On the heels of releasing their new album I Don’t Wanna Say Goodbye, Haywire have lined up a jam-packed live slate for next year. Between January 3 and April 30, the Boston hardcore outfit will play a whopping 80 shows throughout Europe, the UK, and North America. This all follows a late 2026 Australian run including support dates for Rise Against and Dropkick Murphys. All things considered, this may be light work for Haywire, who in 2025 embarked on a DIY tour that hit all 50 states. Find the band’s extensive upcoming itinerary below.
